recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed unless FHIR-I later reopens contained-resource reference semantics.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-I clarification asking whether contained resources can have history, whether contained references may include /_history, and requiring explicit rules that [type]/[id]/_history/[version]#[containedId] can target a contained resource inside a versioned containing resource while [type]/[id]#[containedId]/_history/[version] is invalid and contained resources must use local fragment references to their container or sibling contained resources.
initial_application: Git commit 8db7158a9c0541db6f76f31b0a952c415e2c67f2 explicitly applied FHIR-34345 by adding the contained-resource history and local-reference bullets to source/references.html; later maintenance corrected the original history typo without changing the rule.
additional_context: source/references.html is the authoritative FHIR core references page identified by Jira's related page and is active through source/fhir.ini mappings for Reference and CodeableReference. Current combined-branch source lines 751-755 contain the allowed versioned-container form, the invalid versioned-contained-resource form, and the local fragment reference requirement. A 2019 Zulip thread asked a similar history-version question and is consistent with the rule; Confluence and direct Zulip searches found no conflicting later decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current combined branch already implements the published Jira resolution in build-scope source. The reconciliation published an empty no-change audit commit.

related_jiras.note: The reference regex fragment-support issue is consistent with FHIR-34345's allowed [type]/[id]/_history/[version]#[containedId] reference shape, but it was already represented separately on the combined branch and was not decided here.
